personal_token.label: API key
personal_token.where: Granola desktop app > Settings > Connectors > API keys > Create new key. Tick the note access scopes on the creation screen.
notes: Granola does not publish a fixed key prefix; the field is empty deliberately rather than forgotten.
Requires a Business or Enterprise plan. Any workspace member on those plans can create one; there is no key on the lower tiers at all.

On Enterprise, an admin can restrict which scopes members may use in Settings > Workspace > General > API access for members - so a scope missing from the creation screen is a workspace policy, not a bug.
A personal key is tied to its owner's account and expires. Revoking is permanent and cannot be undone.
There is no sandbox. Test against a small dedicated folder.

workspace_key.label: Workspace API key
workspace_key.where: Granola desktop app > Settings > Connectors > Workspace API keys. Admins only.
notes: Belongs to the workspace rather than a person, does not expire, and keeps working after the admin who made it leaves. The better choice for a workflow that has to keep running.

Reaches public notes, plus any space with 'Allow Granola API access' turned on - which is ON by default for a newly created space, including its folders and subfolders. Worth saying out loud to anyone enabling this.
Cannot read private notes or unshared folders at all.
If the workspace has 'Allow public folders' turned off, public notes are not exposed to the API even with this key.

scopes.personal_notes: Notes the key owner owns, notes shared directly with them, and notes in private folders shared with them.
scopes.public_notes: Notes visible to everyone in the workspace, including the Team space.
scopes.note: Notes are private by default. A note only appears under public_notes if it sits in a folder visible to the whole workspace. Both scopes can be on one key. An empty result is almost always a scope or folder-visibility question rather than an API fault.

pending_operations.note: Granola's overview names what the API returns - meeting notes, transcripts and AI summaries - but not the paths. The reference at docs.granola.ai/introduction has them, along with the base URL and the auth header spelling, and none of it is guessed here.

rate_limits.note: Granola's own figures. Scoped per user or per workspace depending on the key, so a workspace key shared between workflows shares one bucket.

webhooks.note: Granola publishes a webhooks guide covering registration, event subscription, signature verification and retries. Flux has no public endpoint to register, so it polls; recorded so the alternative is not re-derived.

also_ships.mcp: Granola publishes an MCP server that uses browser-based OAuth and is aimed at conversational assistants rather than scripts. Not what this connector uses - an API key is the right shape for a scheduled workflow - but it is the path if a skill ever wants OAuth instead of a pasted key.
